_README: The field inventory each vendor's RENDERED form actually presents, read out of
a live posting on 2026-07-30. Nothing here is inferred or copied from docs.
WHY A STRUCTURAL SNAPSHOT AND NOT SAVED HTML. Saved HTML only works when the
server sends the form. It mostly does not:
breezy   — 35 inputs in the server HTML. Genuine, so breezy.html is kept.
pinpoint — 9 inputs served, 56 in the rendered page. 47 arrive via JS.
personio — 0 inputs served. The whole form is JS.
smartrecruiters — the form lives in 1,806 shadow roots; outerHTML omits it.
A saved file for the last three would LOOK like a fixture and would be a
fiction, and a fiction that passes is worse than no test at all.
WHAT THIS CATCHES: a vendor renaming or dropping a field an adapter targets —
the realistic regression, and the one that would otherwise surface as silently
unfilled applications sent under a real person's name.
WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH: layout changes, a form becoming multi-step, a new
CAPTCHA, or Playwright's locator behaviour. Those need a live run. This is a
cheap guard against the most likely breakage, not a substitute for watching a

breezy.dryRun2026-07-31: All 6 mapped fields matched exactly 1, visible, enabled. cResume required, accept='.pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt, .rtd, .pages'. 'Submit Application' present but ZERO-SIZE on step 1; 'Continue' is the visible control. Same <form> for every step — so field presence after submit proves nothing.

personio.note: Labels are German (Vorname, Nachname, E-Mail) while the name attributes are English. Requiredness is in the label text as '*(erforderlich)', never in the attribute.

pinpoint.note: Rails-nested names. 'Save application for later' sits beside the real submit — matching it would park a draft no employer sees.

smartrecruiters.formUrl: reached via a link whose href contains /oneclick-ui/
smartrecruiters.note: No field carries a name. 1,806 open shadow roots; Playwright pierces them, querySelectorAll does not. Two file inputs share id='file-input' — the résumé one is the LAST, the first is CV-autocomplete.
